## Introduction

`DTAtools` automates the validation of tabular data against **Data Transmission
Agreement (DTA)** and **Data Transmission Specification (DTS)** definitions. In
regulated industries — clinical research, biomarker science, genomics — data
must conform precisely to agreed column types, allowed values, and cross-column
logic before it is transmitted between parties. Catching these errors
programmatically, before submission, saves costly re-submissions and ensures
reproducible, auditable data exchange.

`DTAtools` stores specifications in human-readable **YAML** files and provides
an R API to:

1. **Import** column specifications and semantic rules from YAML (or Word documents),
   reading each column in the type the specification declares for it.
2. **Validate** tabular data against those specifications — types, nullability, allowed values, regex patterns, and cross-column rules.
3. **Inspect** validation results programmatically: which tables failed, which rows, which columns, which rules — and drill into individual errors with `inspect()`.
4. **Export** validated data to files (TSV/CSV, optionally gzip-compressed, with MD5 checksums).
5. **Generate** Word documentation tables directly from specs — for use inside DTA/DTS documents.

Validation reports on three independent axes: **column spec** errors (a value breaks a
column constraint), **rule** errors (a row breaks an inter-column rule), and
**import** errors (a value cannot be represented in the type the specification
declares for its column). See
[Import Errors](#import-errors-values-that-do-not-fit-their-declared-type).

`DTAtools` is built on the S7 object system and uses JSON Schema for fast,
row-level validation.

---

## Installation

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Install from GitHub
remotes::install_github("Boehringer-Ingelheim/DTAtoolsR")
library(DTAtools)
```

```{r}
library(DTAtools)
```

## Package Architecture

`DTAtools` organises objects into a layered hierarchy that maps directly to how
a Data Transmission Specification (DTS) is structured:

<p align="center">
  <img src="DTAtools_architecture.svg" alt="DTAtools package architecture diagram" width="100%"/>
</p>

The same hierarchy, as plain text:

```
DTA                              ← top-level agreement container
├── metadata                     ← title, version, receiver/supplier
|   (DTAMetaData)                     contacts, transmission schedule, ..
│
└── datasets (named list of DTADataSet)  ← one or more datasets per DTS
    │
    ├── DTADataSetTabular        ← tabular data: for tables with
    |   |                            full column-spec + rule validation
    │   ├── files (list)         ← expected file handlers for various
    |   |   |                        input types, manage file names,
    │   │   ├── DTAFileCSV           which can have patterns,
    |   |   ├── DTAFileTSV           number of files, etc ..
    |   |   └── DTAFileDelim
    │   │       └── read_file()  → Arrow Table
    |   |
    │   ├── specs (DTAColumnSpecCollection)  ← column-level specs +
    |   |   |                                   cross-column rules
    │   │   |
    │   │   ├── columns (named list of DTAColumnSpec)
    |   |   |   └── DTAColumnSpec × N   ← one per column: type, nullable,
    │   │   │                            values/pattern, length, format
    |   |   └── rules (list of DTARule)
    │   │       ├── DTARuleColCondition × N  ← if/then cross-column logic
    │   │       ├── DTARuleColRange × N      ← numeric range constraint
    │   │       └── DTARuleColUnique × N     ← uniqueness (single or
    |   |                                              composite key)
    |   |
    │   └── tables (named list)  ← actual data as Arrow Tables
    │       └── <table_name>     ← populated via load_file() or constructor
    │
    └── DTADataSetFile           ← non-tabular: file presence/readability check
        ├── file_paths           ← bound file paths (via load_file() or paths=)
        └── files (list)         ← DTAFileAny descriptors (type: any), which
                                          may restrict the allowed endings
```

**Three ways to build any object, from most to least common:**

1. **`read_dta_from_yaml()`** — a full DTA/DTS (metadata + one or more datasets). The
   recommended entry point for production use — see the Quickstart below.
2. **`read_dataset_from_yaml()`** — a single, self-contained dataset definition
   (name, type, files, columns, rules — no top-level `metadata:`). Ideal when
   you only need to validate one dataset, e.g. while iterating on a spec.
3. **`import_specs_from_yaml()`** — a bare list of column specs (just `columns:`
   plus optional `rules:`, no name/type/files). The most manual option: you
   build the `DTADataSetTabular` wrapper yourself.
4. **Programmatically in R** — construct each class directly (e.g. `DTAColumnSpec()`, `DTADataSetTabular()`)

**Validation flow:**

1. `load_file(dta, dataset, file)` — reads a file into the dataset using its file
   handler, typing each column as the specification declares it
2. `check(dta)` or `check(ds)` — runs the import, JSON Schema and rule checks;
   returns the updated object
3. `results(x)` — one-row-per-table summary (pass/fail, error counts per axis)
4. `messages(x)` — one-row-per-error detail table (`source`, column, row, rule, message, `id`)
5. `inspect(x, id = N)` — deep-dive into a specific error message by its `id`

---

## Quickstart

The canonical production workflow with a full DTA YAML: load the specification,
load the data file, validate, inspect.

```{r quickstart}
library(DTAtools)

# 1. Load the full DTA definition from YAML
#    (metadata + dataset specs + file handlers + rules — all in one file)
dta <- read_dta_from_yaml(
  system.file("extdata", "clinical_dta.yaml", package = "DTAtools")
)
print(dta)

# 2. Load the data file into the DTA object
#    load_file() uses the file handler already defined in the YAML
csv_path <- system.file("extdata", "clinical_data.csv", package = "DTAtools")
dta <- load_file(dta, dataset = "clinical_data", file = csv_path)

# 3. Validate — check() runs column spec + rule validation for all datasets
dta <- check(dta)

# 4. Summarise results (one row per table)
results(dta)
```

### Quickstart Variant: A Single Dataset with `read_dataset_from_yaml()`

Not every delivery needs a full DTA with metadata. When you only need to
validate *one* dataset — while iterating on a spec, or when metadata is
tracked elsewhere — read the dataset definition directly with
`read_dataset_from_yaml()`. This is the second most common entry point into
`DTAtools`, right after `read_dta_from_yaml()`.

A standalone dataset YAML has exactly the same shape as one entry under a
DTA's `datasets:` list — `name`, `type`, `files`, `columns`, `rules` — just
without the surrounding `metadata:`/`datasets:` wrapper. The package ships a
real example of this shape at `inst/extdata/gf_dataset.yaml`; here we build an
equivalent one by extracting the `clinical_data` entry from `clinical_dta.yaml`
so the example stays self-contained:

```{r quickstart_dataset}
# Extract one dataset entry so it stands alone (same shape as gf_dataset.yaml)
full_yaml <- yaml::read_yaml(
  system.file("extdata", "clinical_dta.yaml", package = "DTAtools")
)
dataset_yaml <- tempfile(fileext = ".yaml")
yaml::write_yaml(full_yaml$datasets[[1]], dataset_yaml)

# 1. Load the single-dataset definition — no metadata needed
ds <- read_dataset_from_yaml(dataset_yaml)
ds # a ready-to-use DTADataSetTabular, specs + file handler already set

# 2. Load the data file — same load_file() call as for a full DTA, just
#    without the `dataset =` argument since `ds` already is the dataset
ds <- load_file(ds, file = csv_path, handler_index = 1)

# 3. Validate and summarise — same check()/results() calls as always
ds <- check(ds)
results(ds)

unlink(dataset_yaml)
```

## Column Specifications

### The `DTAColumnSpec` Object

A `DTAColumnSpec` represents a single column's metadata and constraints. It maps
directly to a column entry in a YAML specification.

| Field         | Required | Description                                               |
|---------------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `id`          | ✔        | Column name (must match the data frame header exactly)    |
| `label`       |          | Human-readable label for documentation                   |
| `type`        |          | SAS-style type: `SAS Char`, `SAS Num`, `SAS Int`, `SAS Date`, `SAS Time`, `SAS DateTime` |
| `format`      |          | SAS format string, e.g. `SAS $10.`, `SAS 8.`            |
| `length`      |          | Maximum character length (`maxLength` in JSON Schema)     |
| `nullable`    |          | `TRUE`/`FALSE` — whether the column may be empty/NA      |
| `values`      |          | Closed list of allowed values (`enum` in JSON Schema)    |
| `pattern`     |          | Regular expression every value must match                |
| `description` |          | Free-text description for documentation                  |

> **Note:** `values` and `pattern` are mutually exclusive — a column either has
> a closed value list or a regex pattern, not both.

`type` is not documentation: it decides how the column is *read*. A column
declared `SAS Num` or `SAS Int` is stored as a number, so `"007"` in such a
column becomes `7`; a column declared `SAS Char` is pinned to text, so `"007"`
stays `"007"` even when every value in the file looks numeric. `SAS Date`,
`SAS Time` and `SAS DateTime` are kept as the text that was read and validated
by pattern, so no value is silently re-rendered. `as_r_type()` reports the
mapping:

```{r as_r_type_demo}
vapply(
  c("Char", "Num", "Int", "Date", "Time", "DateTime"),
  function(t) as_r_type(DTAColumnSpecStructureSAS(type = t)),
  character(1)
)
```

```{r column_spec_manual}
# A column with a closed value list
visit_col <- DTAColumnSpec(
  id          = "VISIT",
  label       = "Visit Code",
  type        = "SAS Char",
  length      = 12,
  nullable    = FALSE,
  values      = list("V01", "V02", "V03", "EOT"),
  description = "Planned study visit code"
)
print(visit_col)

# A column with a regex pattern
subjid_col <- DTAColumnSpec(
  id          = "SUBJECT_ID",
  label       = "Subject Identifier",
  type        = "SAS Char",
  nullable    = FALSE,
  pattern     = "^SUBJ[0-9]{4}$",
  description = "Unique subject ID in format SUBJ0001"
)
print(subjid_col)

# A numeric column with no further constraints
age_col <- DTAColumnSpec(
  id       = "AGE",
  label    = "Age (years)",
  type     = "SAS Num",
  nullable = FALSE
)
print(age_col)

# A nullable column (empty / NA allowed)
ae_col <- DTAColumnSpec(
  id       = "AE_TERM",
  label    = "Adverse Event Term",
  type     = "SAS Char",
  nullable = TRUE
)
print(ae_col)
```

### The `DTAColumnSpecCollection` Object

A `DTAColumnSpecCollection` groups column specs together, optionally with a set
of rules. This is the core specs object passed to `DTADataSetTabular`.

```{r spec_collection}
# Build a collection manually
studyid_col <- DTAColumnSpec(
  id = "STUDYID", type = "SAS Char", nullable = FALSE,
  values = list("1234-5678")
)
gender_col <- DTAColumnSpec(
  id = "GENDER", type = "SAS Char", nullable = FALSE,
  values = list("Male", "Female", "Other")
)

specs <- DTAColumnSpecCollection(
  columns = list(
    STUDYID = studyid_col,
    VISIT   = visit_col,
    AGE     = age_col,
    GENDER  = gender_col,
    AE_TERM = ae_col
  )
)
print(specs)

# Access individual column specs
names(specs)
colspec(specs, "VISIT")
```

### Use Case 3: Bare Specs with `import_specs_from_yaml()`

`read_dta_from_yaml()` and `read_dataset_from_yaml()` (both shown in the
Quickstart above) cover the vast majority of use cases. The third, most manual
option is `import_specs_from_yaml()`: it reads *only* the `columns` key (plus
an optional `rules` key) from a YAML file — ignoring any `name`, `type`, or
`files` keys — and returns a bare `DTAColumnSpecCollection` with no dataset
wrapper. Use it when you already manage the data table and dataset naming
yourself and just need the column/rule definitions, e.g. to build a
`DTADataSetTabular` by hand as shown further below.

```{r import_yaml}
# The package ships with a real standalone dataset YAML — import_specs_from_yaml()
# reads only its `columns`/`rules` keys, ignoring name/type/files
yaml_file <- system.file("extdata", "gf_dataset.yaml", package = "DTAtools")
gf_specs <- import_specs_from_yaml(yaml_file)
print(gf_specs)
```

The resulting object contains both columns and rules:

```{r inspect_specs}
# How many columns?
length(gf_specs@columns)

# Look at an individual spec by column ID
colspec(gf_specs, "GFSTAT")

# Are there rules?
gf_specs@rules
```

> **Nested YAML:** If your specs live inside a larger YAML file under a nested
> key (e.g. under `DTA: format:`), pass `tag = c("DTA", "format")` to
> `import_specs_from_yaml()`.

### Exporting Specifications to YAML and JSON

Specifications can be serialised back to YAML or JSON, making it easy to share,
version-control, or programmatically generate specs.

```{r export_specs_yaml}
# Write to YAML
yaml_out <- tempfile(fileext = ".yaml")
write_columns_to_yaml(gf_specs, yaml_out)
cat(paste(readLines(yaml_out, n = 20), collapse = "\n"))
unlink(yaml_out)
```

```{r export_specs_json}
# Write to JSON
json_out <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
write_columns_to_json(gf_specs, json_out)
cat(paste(readLines(json_out, n = 25), collapse = "\n"))
unlink(json_out)
```

## Data Validation

### Creating a `DTADataSetTabular`

A `DTADataSetTabular` combines a `DTAColumnSpecCollection` with one or more
data tables. Tables are stored internally as Arrow Tables for performance.

```{r create_dataset}
# Load the clinical DTA specs from a full DTA YAML (metadata + datasets)
clinical_yaml <- system.file("extdata", "clinical_dta.yaml", package = "DTAtools")
dta_obj <- read_dta_from_yaml(clinical_yaml)

# The DTA contains one dataset called "clinical_data" — but tables are empty
# until you load data into them
datasets(dta_obj)
ds_spec <- datasets(dta_obj, "clinical_data")
ds_spec # specs defined, no tables yet
```

The most flexible approach is to combine specs with your own data:

```{r load_data_into_ds}
# Get specs from the full DTA spec
clinical_specs <- specs(ds_spec)

# Read the CSV independently
csv_path <- system.file("extdata", "clinical_data.csv", package = "DTAtools")
raw_data <- read.csv(csv_path)

# Create the DTADataSetTabular with specs + data, then validate
ds <- DTADataSetTabular(
  name   = "clinical_data",
  specs  = clinical_specs,
  tables = list(clinical_data = raw_data)
)
ds
```

Alternatively, create a dataset directly in R with inline data:

```{r inline_dataset}
# Build specs
col_studyid <- DTAColumnSpec(
  id = "STUDYID", type = "SAS Char", nullable = FALSE,
  values = list("STUDY001")
)
col_visit <- DTAColumnSpec(
  id = "VISIT", type = "SAS Char", nullable = FALSE,
  values = list("SCREENING", "BASELINE", "WEEK4")
)
col_age <- DTAColumnSpec(id = "AGE", type = "SAS Num", nullable = FALSE)

inline_specs <- DTAColumnSpecCollection(
  columns = list(STUDYID = col_studyid, VISIT = col_visit, AGE = col_age)
)

# Build data
inline_data <- data.frame(
  STUDYID = c("STUDY001", "STUDY001", "STUDY001"),
  VISIT   = c("SCREENING", "BASELINE", "WEEK4"),
  AGE     = c(32, 32, 32)
)

# Combine into a DTADataSetTabular
inline_ds <- DTADataSetTabular(
  name   = "inline_example",
  specs  = inline_specs,
  tables = list(my_table = inline_data)
)
inline_ds
```

### Validating with `check()`

`check()` reports on three independent axes:

1. **Import errors** — a value that cannot be represented in the type its column
   declares. The value is stored as `NA` and the original text is retained. See
   [Import Errors](#import-errors-values-that-do-not-fit-their-declared-type).
2. **Column spec errors** — JSON Schema validation of every row against column types,
   `nullable`, `values`, `pattern`, and `length`.
3. **Rule errors** — inter-column rules (`col_condition`, `col_range`,
   `col_unique`).

All three are always evaluated, and a failure on any one of them fails the
table. `check()` **always returns the updated object** — assign the result back.

Useful arguments:

| Argument       | Default | Description                                                              |
|----------------|---------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `force`        | `FALSE` | Revalidate even when neither the data nor the specs have changed         |
| `persist`      | `TRUE`  | Write a validation artifact per table, readable later by `validation_errors()` |
| `artifact_dir` | `NULL`  | Where those artifacts go; defaults to a per-dataset directory under `tempdir()` |
| `quiet`        | `FALSE` | Suppress the console report                                              |
| `tables`       | `NULL`  | Restrict validation to named or indexed tables (`datasets` on a `DTA`)   |

Without `force`, a table whose data and specs hash unchanged is skipped and its
previous result is reused. Pass `check(x, force = TRUE)` to bypass that shortcut
and re-validate every table regardless.

#### Validating a dataset

```{r validate_ds}
ds <- check(ds)
```

### Inspecting Validation Results

After `check()`, use these functions to inspect what happened:

| Function              | Returns                                                   |
|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `results(x)`          | One row per table: status, per-axis error counts, timestamps |
| `messages(x)`         | One row per error: `id`, `source`, column, row, rule, message |
| `validation_status(x)`| Compact status table, one row per table                    |
| `validation_errors(x, table)` | The full stored detail object for one table; `as.data.frame()` gives one row per reported error |

`validation_status()` returns exactly these columns: `table`, `target_type`,
`status`, `ok`, `validated_at`, `run_id`, `validation_run`, `n_columnspec_errors`,
`n_rule_errors`, `n_import_errors`. `results()` returns the same per-axis counts
plus `dataset`, `target` and the roll-up columns `n_targets`, `n_validated`,
`n_valid`, `n_invalid`, `n_skipped`, `n_not_validated`.

`n_import_errors` is `NA` rather than `0` when the recorded result predates the
import axis — unknown, not zero. `messages()` returns a warning row saying as
much, and `check(x, force = TRUE)` re-validates to replace the stale artifact.

```{r inspect_results}
# Summary per table
results(ds)

# Detailed per-error messages (empty for a passing dataset)
msgs <- messages(ds)
head(msgs)
```

### Drilling into Errors with `inspect()`

`messages()` gives you a row per error with an `id` column. When you want the
full story behind a specific error — the exact cell value, the row in context,
the JSON Schema constraint that failed, or the rows that violated a rule —
call `inspect(x, id = N)`.

```
results(x)     → per-table pass/fail summary
messages(x)    → per-error table — note the `id` of the error you care about
inspect(x, id) → deep detail for that error: row context, column spec clause, failing rows
```

`inspect()` returns a flat data frame. Every row carries `id`, `source`, `type`,
`message` and `why`; the remaining columns depend on which axis the error came
from, and are prefixed by that axis:

| Source   | Key columns added by `inspect()`                                              |
|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `import` | `import_row`, `import_column`, `import_raw` (the original text), `import_declared_type`, `import_reason` |
| `columnspec` | `context_*` (the actual row values), `columnspec_keyword`, `columnspec_message`       |
| `rule`   | `rule_id`, `failing_row_count`, `failing_*` (preview of violating rows)       |

Because the columns differ by source, select the `id` you want by source rather
than assuming a position. `messages()` is sorted by dataset, target, source and
row, so `id = 1` is an import error whenever the table has one.

```{r inspect_example}
# Load a dataset that has column spec errors
err_file <- system.file("extdata", "clinical_data_error_columnspec.csv", package = "DTAtools")
dta_err <- read_dta_from_yaml(
  system.file("extdata", "clinical_dta.yaml", package = "DTAtools")
)
dta_err <- load_file(dta_err, "clinical_data", file = err_file)
dta_err <- check(dta_err, quiet = TRUE)

# Step 1: see which messages exist and note their ids and sources
ds_err_loaded <- datasets(dta_err, "clinical_data")
msgs_err <- messages(ds_err_loaded)
head(msgs_err[, c("id", "source", "row", "column", "message")], 8)
```

```{r inspect_columnspec}
# Step 2: inspect a column spec error — pick the first id whose source is "columnspec"
columnspec_id <- msgs_err$id[msgs_err$source == "columnspec"][1]
detail <- inspect(ds_err_loaded, id = columnspec_id)
# Key fields for column spec errors:
detail[, c(
  "id", "message", "type", "why",
  "context_.row", "context_SUBJECT_ID", "context_VISIT",
  "columnspec_keyword", "columnspec_message"
)]
```

```{r inspect_rule}
# Rule errors: inspect shows which rows violated the rule
rule_file <- system.file("extdata", "clinical_data_error_rules.csv", package = "DTAtools")
dta_rule <- read_dta_from_yaml(
  system.file("extdata", "clinical_dta.yaml", package = "DTAtools")
)
dta_rule <- load_file(dta_rule, "clinical_data", file = rule_file)
dta_rule <- check(dta_rule, quiet = TRUE)

ds_rule_loaded <- datasets(dta_rule, "clinical_data")
msgs_rule <- messages(ds_rule_loaded)
msgs_rule[, c("id", "source", "rule_id", "message")]

# Drill into the first rule violation
rule_id_1 <- msgs_rule$id[msgs_rule$source == "rule"][1]
detail_rule <- inspect(ds_rule_loaded, id = rule_id_1)
detail_rule[, c(
  "id", "rule_id", "type", "why",
  "failing_row_count", "failing_.row",
  "failing_SUBJECT_ID", "failing_VISIT"
)]
```

### Example: Column Spec Errors

The package ships with a CSV that deliberately violates several column
constraints. The error file has:

- A missing `HEIGHT` column (required by spec, since `nullable: false`)
- An invalid `GENDER` value `"Alien"` (not in the allowed list)
- A non-numeric `BMI` cell, `"heavy"`, in a `SAS Num` column
- An invalid `STUDYID` `"9999-9999"` (not in allowed values)
- A `VISIT` value that exceeds the `length: 12` constraint

Note that the `BMI` cell is reported twice, on two different axes: once as an
import error, because `"heavy"` is not a number and became `NA`, and once as a
column spec error, because the resulting `NA` fails a `nullable: false` column. The
counts in `results()` reflect that — `n_import_errors` and `n_columnspec_errors` are
counted separately and neither subsumes the other.

```{r columnspec_errors}
dta_obj_e <- read_dta_from_yaml(
  system.file("extdata", "clinical_dta.yaml", package = "DTAtools")
)
err_file <- system.file("extdata", "clinical_data_error_columnspec.csv", package = "DTAtools")
raw_err <- read.csv(err_file)

ds_err <- DTADataSetTabular(
  name   = "clinical_data",
  specs  = specs(datasets(dta_obj_e, "clinical_data")),
  tables = list(clinical_data = raw_err)
)
ds_err <- check(ds_err)

# See which tables failed
results(ds_err)

# Get the individual error messages (first 10)
msgs_err <- messages(ds_err)
head(msgs_err[, c("target", "source", "row", "column", "message")], 10)
```

### Example: Schema Rule Violations

This CSV has valid column values but violates semantic rules:

- `CONSENT = "YES"` but `CONSENT_DATE` is empty (`rule_dependency_example`)
- `VISIT = "V03"` but `STATUS = "DROPPED"` (`rule_equal_example`)
- `AGE = 70`, outside the allowed range 18–65 (`rule_range_example`)
- `SUBJECT_ID + VISIT` combination is not unique (`rule_unique_example`)
- `WEIGHT < 5` when `VISIT = V03` (`check_col_condition_example`)

```{r rule_errors}
dta_obj_r <- read_dta_from_yaml(
  system.file("extdata", "clinical_dta.yaml", package = "DTAtools")
)
rule_file <- system.file("extdata", "clinical_data_error_rules.csv", package = "DTAtools")
raw_rule <- read.csv(rule_file)

ds_rule <- DTADataSetTabular(
  name   = "clinical_data",
  specs  = specs(datasets(dta_obj_r, "clinical_data")),
  tables = list(clinical_data = raw_rule)
)
ds_rule <- check(ds_rule)

results(ds_rule)
messages(ds_rule)[, c("target", "source", "rule_id", "message")]
```

## Import Errors: Values That Do Not Fit Their Declared Type

An **import error** is a value that is present in the source but cannot be
represented in the type its column declares. Reading a `SAS Num` column whose
file contains `"unknown"` is the canonical case.

When this happens, three things follow:

1. The stored value becomes `NA`. The column keeps its declared type, so one bad
   cell does not turn a whole numeric column into text.
2. The original text is retained and reported, so nothing is lost silently.
3. The table fails validation. **Any import error makes validation fail**, on
   its own, even when every column spec constraint and every rule passes.

The third point is the one that surprises: a file can fail without a single
column spec or rule error against it. That is not a false positive — it means a
value could not be represented in its declared type and would otherwise have
been quietly discarded.

### A minimal example

The specification below declares `AGE` as `SAS Num` and permits missing values.
The data contains the text `"unknown"`. Nothing violates the column specs, and there
are no rules at all, yet the table fails:

```{r import_minimal}
import_specs2 <- DTAColumnSpecCollection(columns = list(
  SUBJECT_ID = DTAColumnSpec(id = "SUBJECT_ID", type = "SAS Char", nullable = FALSE),
  AGE        = DTAColumnSpec(id = "AGE", type = "SAS Num", nullable = TRUE)
))

import_data <- data.frame(
  SUBJECT_ID = c("SUBJ0001", "SUBJ0002"),
  AGE        = c("34", "unknown")
)

ds_import <- DTADataSetTabular(
  name   = "import_demo",
  specs  = import_specs2,
  tables = list(demo = import_data)
)
ds_import <- check(ds_import, quiet = TRUE)

validation_status(ds_import)[, c(
  "status", "ok", "n_columnspec_errors",
  "n_rule_errors", "n_import_errors"
)]
```

The three axes are independent: `n_columnspec_errors` and `n_rule_errors` are `0`,
`n_import_errors` is `1`, and `ok` is `FALSE`.

> **Reading the console output.** `check()` prints a per-axis report for the
> column spec and rule passes but not for the import pass, so a table that fails on
> the import axis alone shows `Table format, length, pattern, and values are
> valid` followed by `0 of 1 table valid`. Consult `n_import_errors` — or
> `messages()` — rather than the banner when a table fails for no visible
> reason.

### Finding the value that caused it

Import errors appear in `messages()` with `source == "import"`, and the `keyword`
column carries the reason:

```{r import_messages}
imp <- messages(ds_import)
imp[imp$source == "import", c("id", "row", "column", "keyword", "message")]
```

`inspect()` gives the structured version, including `import_raw` — the original
text exactly as it was read:

```{r import_inspect}
import_id <- imp$id[imp$source == "import"][1]
detail_imp <- inspect(ds_import, id = import_id)
detail_imp[, c(
  "import_row", "import_column", "import_raw",
  "import_declared_type", "import_reason"
)]
```

The stored table holds `NA` in that cell, and the column is numeric as declared:

```{r import_stored_value}
as.data.frame(get_table(ds_import, "demo"))
```

Two reasons are reported:

| `reason` / `keyword` | Meaning                                                                 |
|----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `not_convertible`    | No part of the value fits the declared type, e.g. `"unknown"` as a number |
| `trailing_residue`   | A prefix of the value fits and the remainder would be dropped, e.g. `"2026-12-31 at the earliest"` as a date |

### Import errors in metadata

Metadata is validated on the same axis. A transmission date written with a
qualification cannot be stored as a date without discarding the qualification,
so it is recorded as an import error and fails the whole `DTA`:

```{r import_metadata}
meta_bad <- DTAMetaData(
  title        = "Qualified transmission date",
  version      = "1.0",
  transmission = list(date_first_transfer = "2026-12-31 at the earliest")
)

metadata_import_errors(meta_bad)
```

`metadata_import_errors()` returns the same five columns as the table-level
frame, with `column` naming the metadata field path rather than a data column.

## Rules

Rules are defined alongside column specs and express inter-column
constraints that cannot be captured by JSON Schema alone.

### Rule Types

#### `col_condition` — If/Then Logic

The most versatile rule type. When `condition` is satisfied for a row, the
`then` block is enforced on that same row.

**Supported operators in both `condition` and `then`:**

| Operator        | Applies to        | Example                          |
|-----------------|-------------------|----------------------------------|
| `equals`        | string / number   | `equals: "YES"`                  |
| `not_equals`    | string / number   | `not_equals: "DROPPED"`          |
| `empty`         | any (`true/false`)| `empty: true`                    |
| `in`            | list              | `in: [V01, V02, EOT]`            |
| `not_in`        | list              | `not_in: [REJECTED]`             |
| `pattern`       | string regex      | `pattern: "^SUBJ[0-9]{4}$"`     |
| `greater`       | number            | `greater: 0`                     |
| `greater_equal` | number            | `greater_equal: 18`              |
| `less`          | number            | `less: 200`                      |
| `less_equal`    | number            | `less_equal: 65`                 |
| `min` / `max`   | number range      | `min: 10` + `max: 100`           |

```yaml
rules:
  # IF consent was given, consent date must be filled in
  - id: consent_requires_date
    type: col_condition
    condition:
      CONSENT:
        equals: "YES"
    then:
      CONSENT_DATE:
        empty: false

  # IF visit is V03, status must be COMPLETED
  - id: v03_must_be_completed
    type: col_condition
    condition:
      VISIT:
        equals: V03
    then:
      STATUS:
        equals: COMPLETED

  # IF sample has no reason for test not done, result must be present
  - id: result_when_no_reason
    type: col_condition
    condition:
      GFREASND:
        empty: true
    then:
      GFORRES:
        empty: false

  # Multiple conditions and multiple then-clauses are fully supported
  - id: v03_full_check
    type: col_condition
    condition:
      VISIT:
        equals: V03
    then:
      STATUS:
        equals: COMPLETED
      AGE:
        min: 18
        max: 65
      WEIGHT:
        greater_equal: 5
```

#### `col_range` — Numeric Range Check

Enforces that all values in a numeric column fall within `[min, max]`.

```yaml
rules:
  - id: age_range
    type: col_range
    column: AGE
    min: 18
    max: 65
```

#### `col_unique` — Uniqueness Constraint

Enforces that all combinations of values across one or more columns are unique.
Specifying multiple columns checks the combined key for uniqueness.

```yaml
rules:
  # Single column uniqueness
  - id: subject_unique
    type: col_unique
    column: SUBJECT_ID

  # Composite key uniqueness: SUBJECT_ID + VISIT must be unique per row
  - id: subject_visit_unique
    type: col_unique
    column:
      - SUBJECT_ID
      - VISIT
```

#### `group_condition` — Group-Level Constraints

`group_condition` is distinct from the other rule types: instead of evaluating
each row independently, it first groups rows by one or more columns and then
applies constraint logic *across the whole group*. This makes it possible to
express rules that span multiple rows for the same entity — for example, "if
any row in this subject's group records consent, then every row in that group
must supply a consent date."

A `group_condition` rule has three required parts:

- **`group_by`** — columns that define the group (e.g. `SUBJECT_ID`, or a
  composite key like `[SUBJIDN, VISIT]`).
- **`conditions`** — named Boolean flags. Each condition maps a name (e.g.
  `c_consent_yes`) to a column test in the same operator syntax used by
  `col_condition` (`equals`, `empty`, `in`, …). A condition evaluates to
  `TRUE` for a row when all of its column tests pass.
- **`constraints`** — rules over the named condition flags. Two constraint
  types are supported:

| Type | Aliases | Meaning |
|------|---------|---------|
| `requires` | `implies` | IF condition `if` holds (per `if_scope`), THEN condition `then` must hold (per `then_scope`) |
| `mutually_exclusive` | `not_both` | conditions `left` and `right` cannot both be true within the same group |

The `if_scope` / `then_scope` (or `left_scope` / `right_scope`) fields control
how the condition is aggregated over the rows in a group:

| Scope | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `any` (default) | At least one row in the group satisfies the condition |
| `all` | Every row in the group satisfies the condition |

```yaml
rules:
  # ── requires: IF any row in the group has CONSENT="YES",
  #              THEN all rows in the group must have a CONSENT_DATE ──────────
  - id: consent_requires_date_per_subject
    type: group_condition
    group_by:
      - SUBJECT_ID
    conditions:
      c_consent_yes:
        CONSENT:
          equals: "YES"
      c_consent_date_present:
        CONSENT_DATE:
          empty: false
    constraints:
      - id: consent_needs_date
        type: requires          # alias: implies
        if: c_consent_yes
        then: c_consent_date_present
        if_scope: any           # true when ANY row in the group matches
        then_scope: all         # requires ALL rows in the group to match

  # ── mutually_exclusive: failed QC and reported result are incompatible ─────
  - id: failed_vs_reported
    type: group_condition
    group_by:
      - SUBJIDN
      - VISIT
    conditions:
      c_failed:
        GFREASND:
          empty: false          # a failure reason is present
      c_reported:
        GFREASND:
          empty: true
        GFORRES:
          empty: false          # a numeric result is present and no failure reason
    constraints:
      - id: qc_fail_and_result_are_exclusive
        type: mutually_exclusive    # alias: not_both
        left: c_failed
        right: c_reported
```

> **When to use `group_condition` vs `col_condition`:** `col_condition` checks
> each row in isolation. Use `group_condition` when the rule depends on the
> combination of rows that share the same grouping key — e.g. all rows for one
> subject, or all rows for one sample-at-one-visit.

### Defining Rules in R

Rules can also be constructed programmatically:

```{r rules_in_R}
# col_range rule
range_rule <- DTARuleColRange(id = "age_range", columns = "AGE", min = 18, max = 65)

# col_unique rule (composite key)
unique_rule <- DTARuleColUnique(id = "subject_visit_unique", columns = c("SUBJECT_ID", "VISIT"))

# col_condition rule: IF CONSENT == "YES" THEN CONSENT_DATE must not be empty
condition_rule <- DTARuleColCondition(
  id        = "consent_requires_date",
  condition = list(CONSENT = list(equals = "YES")),
  then      = list(CONSENT_DATE = list(empty = FALSE))
)

# group_condition rule: IF any row in the subject group has CONSENT="YES",
#                       THEN all rows in the group must have a CONSENT_DATE
group_rule <- DTARuleGroupCondition(
  id = "consent_requires_date_per_subject",
  group_by = "SUBJECT_ID",
  conditions = list(
    c_consent_yes          = list(CONSENT = list(equals = "YES")),
    c_consent_date_present = list(CONSENT_DATE = list(empty = FALSE))
  ),
  constraints = list(
    list(
      id         = "consent_needs_date",
      type       = "requires",
      `if`       = "c_consent_yes",
      `then`     = "c_consent_date_present",
      if_scope   = "any",
      then_scope = "all"
    )
  )
)

# Collect rules in a plain list
rule_collection <- list(range_rule, unique_rule, condition_rule, group_rule)
```

```{r specs_with_rules}
# Attach rules to a DTAColumnSpecCollection
studyid <- DTAColumnSpec(
  id = "STUDYID", type = "SAS Char", nullable = FALSE,
  values = list("STUDY001")
)
visit2 <- DTAColumnSpec(
  id = "VISIT", type = "SAS Char", nullable = FALSE,
  values = list("SCREENING", "BASELINE", "WEEK4")
)
age2 <- DTAColumnSpec(id = "AGE", type = "SAS Num", nullable = FALSE)
consent <- DTAColumnSpec(
  id = "CONSENT", type = "SAS Char", nullable = TRUE,
  values = list("YES", "NO")
)
con_date <- DTAColumnSpec(id = "CONSENT_DATE", type = "SAS Char", nullable = TRUE)
subjid2 <- DTAColumnSpec(id = "SUBJECT_ID", type = "SAS Char", nullable = FALSE)

specs_with_rules <- DTAColumnSpecCollection(
  columns = list(
    STUDYID = studyid, VISIT = visit2, AGE = age2,
    CONSENT = consent, CONSENT_DATE = con_date, SUBJECT_ID = subjid2
  ),
  rules = rule_collection
)
print(specs_with_rules)

# Validate data that violates the rules
bad_data <- data.frame(
  STUDYID      = c("STUDY001", "STUDY001"),
  VISIT        = c("SCREENING", "BASELINE"),
  AGE          = c(16, 32), # 16 violates age_range (min 18)
  CONSENT      = c("YES", "NO"),
  CONSENT_DATE = c(NA, NA), # CONSENT=YES but no date: violates consent_requires_date
  SUBJECT_ID   = c("P01", "P01") # duplicate SUBJECT_ID: violates subject_visit_unique when VISIT differs too
)

ds_bad <- DTADataSetTabular(
  name   = "demo_rules",
  specs  = specs_with_rules,
  tables = list(demo = bad_data)
)
ds_bad <- check(ds_bad)

messages(ds_bad)[, c("source", "rule_id", "row", "column", "message")]
```

## Compressed Input Files

A gzipped file needs no special handling. Arrow decompresses `.gz` while
reading, and a file handler that declares `clinical_data2.csv` accepts
`clinical_data2.csv.gz` — compression describes how the file travelled, not
what it contains, so the specification never mentions it.

```{r gzip-input}
handler <- DTAFileCSV("clinical_data2.csv")

matches_filename(handler, "clinical_data2.csv")
matches_filename(handler, "clinical_data2.csv.gz")

plain <- as.data.frame(read_file(
  handler,
  system.file("extdata", "clinical_data2.csv", package = "DTAtools")
))
gzipped <- as.data.frame(read_file(
  handler,
  system.file("extdata", "clinical_data2.csv.gz", package = "DTAtools")
))

identical(plain, gzipped)
```

The same holds for an anchored pattern (`^clinical_data2\.csv$` matches the
gzipped form), for `check()`, and for `validate_file_stream()` — a compressed
file is still scanned in batches rather than expanded into memory, and the row
numbers it reports are positions in the file.

Only gzip is claimed. Arrow can read other codecs, but accepting a suffix here
that the reader then fails on would trade a clear "no file matched" for an
opaque Arrow error.

## Validating a File Too Large to Load

Everything above reads the data into memory before checking it. For a file
larger than the memory available that is not merely slow — it is impossible,
because the table has to exist as an R object before a single row can be
validated.

The answer is to scan the file in batches, holding one batch at a time. There
are two ways to ask for that: through the object model, or standalone.

### Choosing at load time

`load_file()` takes a `stream` argument that decides how the table is *held*
once loaded. `"never"` reads it into memory as an Arrow `Table`, `"always"`
keeps it as a lazy Arrow `Dataset` that `check()` scans in batches, and the
default `"auto"` picks between them on the file's size on disk:

```{r stream-load-file}
stream_dta_path <- system.file("extdata", "clinical_dta.yaml", package = "DTAtools")
stream_csv <- system.file("extdata", "clinical_data.csv", package = "DTAtools")

eager_dta <- load_file(read_dta_from_yaml(stream_dta_path), 1,
  file = stream_csv, stream = "never"
)
lazy_dta <- load_file(read_dta_from_yaml(stream_dta_path), 1,
  file = stream_csv, stream = "always"
)

# The same file, held two different ways.
c(
  eager = class(tables(eager_dta@datasets[[1]])[["clinical_data"]])[[1]],
  lazy  = class(tables(lazy_dta@datasets[[1]])[["clinical_data"]])[[1]]
)
```

Both reach the same verdict — `check()` scans the lazy one and materialises
nothing:

```{r stream-load-file-check}
eager_res <- results(check(eager_dta, quiet = TRUE, persist = FALSE))
lazy_res <- results(check(lazy_dta, quiet = TRUE, persist = FALSE))

identical(
  eager_res[, c("status", "n_columnspec_errors", "n_rule_errors", "n_import_errors")],
  lazy_res[, c("status", "n_columnspec_errors", "n_rule_errors", "n_import_errors")]
)
```

What differs is *when* import errors are found. Reading into memory coerces the
columns during `load_file()` and records the issues there and then; the lazy
path has no rows yet, so its issues appear during `check()`. After a streaming
load the dataset's `@import_issues` is empty until the check has run — the same
issues, found later.

`TRUE` and `FALSE` work as aliases for `"always"` and `"never"`, and the
session-wide default and threshold are options:

```{r stream-options, eval = FALSE}
options(DTAtools.stream = "always") # or "never" / "auto"
options(DTAtools.stream_threshold = 2 * 1024^3) # bytes; default 512 MB
```

`"auto"` accounts for compression: a `.csv.gz`'s on-disk size is multiplied by
an expansion estimate (4×) before the comparison, so a compressed table large
enough to matter streams by default. Either explicit `stream` value still
overrides the guess.

`check()` takes the two scan knobs, both ignored for a table already in memory:
`batch_rows` (rows per batch, default
`getOption("DTAtools.stream_batch_rows", 131072L)`) and `max_errors` (how much
per-cell detail is held in RAM — it changes neither the counts nor the
verdict, and rows past the cap spill to a session-temporary store that
`collect_full_errors()` reassembles).

### Choosing between them

| Situation | Use | Why |
|---|---|---|
| The file fits in memory comfortably | `"never"`, or the default | About twice as fast, and import errors are reported at load |
| The file is larger than memory, or close to it | `"always"` | The only option that works at all |
| You will validate the same table many times | `"never"` | Every scan re-parses from disk; an in-memory table is parsed once |
| A large compressed file (`.csv.gz`) | `"auto"` handles it | The size test multiplies a `.gz`'s on-disk bytes by an expansion estimate |
| You just want a verdict, with no `DTA` object | `validate_file_stream()` | Same scan, without the object model |
| You do not know, and sizes vary | `"auto"` (the default) | Small files stay fast; a file that would not fit switches by itself |

The short version: stream when *holding* the file is the problem. What follows
makes that concrete — what the scan bounds, and what it costs.

### Scanning without a DTA object

`validate_file_stream()` does the same scan given only the specs and a path,
returning the details list directly. It opens the file as a lazy Arrow dataset
and never holds more than one batch at a time.

```{r stream-basic}
stream_specs <- DTAColumnSpecCollection(
  columns = list(
    ID  = DTAColumnSpec(id = "ID", type = "SAS Char", length = 4, nullable = FALSE),
    AGE = DTAColumnSpec(id = "AGE", type = "SAS Num", nullable = TRUE)
  ),
  rules = list(DTARuleColRange(id = "age_range", columns = "AGE", range = c(18, 70)))
)

stream_path <- file.path(tempdir(), "vignette_stream.csv")
utils::write.csv(
  data.frame(
    ID  = c("A001", "TOOLONG", "B002"),
    AGE = c(30, 40, 99)
  ),
  stream_path,
  row.names = FALSE
)

details <- validate_file_stream(stream_specs, stream_path, verbose = FALSE)
c(ok = details$ok, columnspec = details$n_columnspec_errors, rules = details$n_rule_errors)
```

The result carries the same three-axis structure `check()` produces, and
flattens to one row per error:

```{r stream-messages}
as.data.frame(details)[, c("source", "row", "column", "keyword")]
```

### What is bounded, and what is not

Nothing in the scan grows with the number of rows:

| what | bounded by |
|------|------------|
| column-spec checks | the batch size |
| range and if/then rules | the batch size |
| uniqueness rules (text keys) | Arrow's engine — the distinct keys never enter R |
| uniqueness rules (other keys) | the number of distinct keys |
| grouped rules | the number of distinct groups |
| error detail held in RAM | `max_errors` (the rest spills to disk, nothing is lost) |

Measured across a sixteen-fold increase in input, the working set held by the
scan stayed flat at about 19 MB, while the in-memory path's grew from 51 MB to
272 MB.

**This buys feasibility, not speed.** Scanning runs roughly twice as slow as
validating a table already in memory, because each batch pays its own dispatch
and typing overhead. Use it when *holding* the file is the problem; for a file
that fits comfortably, `check()` is faster and there is nothing to gain here.

### Stopping early

Two options change how much work the scan does.

`fail_fast = TRUE` stops at the first batch that shows a problem. On a large
file that fails early this is the difference between seconds and hours:

```{r stream-failfast}
quick <- validate_file_stream(
  stream_specs, stream_path,
  fail_fast = TRUE, verbose = FALSE
)
c(ok = quick$ok, partial = isTRUE(attr(quick, "partial_scan")))
```

A stopped scan is explicitly incomplete. It carries a `partial_scan` attribute,
lists only the rules that actually failed, and reports `NA` — not `TRUE` — for
any axis it could not settle. A rule that has not failed yet has not passed: a
duplicate further into the file was simply never read.

`on_missing_column = "stop"` uses the fact that a missing column is decidable
from the header alone. The default, `"scan"`, reads the file and reports the
absence once per row — faithful, but on a 400-million-row file that restates
one fact 400 million times.

```{r stream-structural}
missing_specs <- DTAColumnSpecCollection(
  columns = list(
    ID      = DTAColumnSpec(id = "ID", type = "SAS Char", length = 4, nullable = FALSE),
    ABSENT  = DTAColumnSpec(id = "ABSENT", type = "SAS Char", length = 4, nullable = FALSE)
  )
)

structural <- validate_file_stream(
  missing_specs, stream_path,
  on_missing_column = "stop", verbose = FALSE
)
structural$columnspec_errors$full_error[, c("keyword", "message")]
```

Columns present in the file but absent from the specs are reported too — the
per-row checks have no way to notice a column no spec describes.

### Caching as Parquet

`cache_as_parquet()` rewrites a delimited file as Parquet, streaming, so
repeated validations read a columnar format instead of re-parsing text.

Measure before adopting it. On a 500,000-row file of 20 columns where the specs
read every column, validating from the cache was *not* faster — evaluating the
constraints dominates, and a format that only makes reading cheaper cannot move
a cost that is not there. The case it should win, a wide file where the specs
read only a few columns, is untested; `benchmarks/bench_parquet.R` reports the
break-even for your own data.

```{r stream-cleanup, include=FALSE}
unlink(stream_path)
```

## File-based Workflow

When the DTA defines expected files, use `DTAFileCSV` (or `DTAFileTSV`,
`DTAFileDelim`) as file handlers inside the dataset. The `read_file()` function
reads data through the handler, returning an Arrow Table you can pass directly
to `DTADataSetTabular`.

```{r file_workflow}
# Create a CSV file handler — describes the expected file format
file_handler <- DTAFileCSV(filename = "clinical_data.csv")

# Show what the handler captures
print(file_handler)

# Read the actual file through the handler
csv_path <- system.file("extdata", "clinical_data.csv", package = "DTAtools")
tbl <- read_file(file_handler, csv_path)
cat("Loaded table class:", class(tbl)[1], "\n")
cat("Dimensions:", nrow(tbl), "x", ncol(tbl), "\n")

# The Arrow Table can be passed directly to DTADataSetTabular
simple_specs <- DTAColumnSpecCollection(columns = list(
  STUDYID = DTAColumnSpec(
    id = "STUDYID", type = "SAS Char", nullable = FALSE,
    values = list("1234-5678")
  ),
  VISIT = DTAColumnSpec(
    id = "VISIT", type = "SAS Char", nullable = FALSE,
    values = list("V01", "V02", "V03", "EOT")
  ),
  AGE = DTAColumnSpec(id = "AGE", type = "SAS Num", nullable = FALSE)
))

# Use the Arrow Table directly in the constructor
ds_from_file <- DTADataSetTabular(
  name   = "clinical_from_file",
  specs  = simple_specs,
  files  = list(file_handler), # document the expected file
  tables = list(clinical_data = tbl) # provide the loaded data
)
names(tables(ds_from_file)) # the table names held by the dataset
```

For full DTA YAML specs that include file definitions, the file handlers are
embedded in each dataset specification and can be retrieved with `files()`:

```{r file_handlers_from_dta}
dta_spec <- read_dta_from_yaml(
  system.file("extdata", "clinical_dta.yaml", package = "DTAtools")
)
ds_s <- datasets(dta_spec, "clinical_data")

# Inspect the file handler defined in the YAML
fh <- files(ds_s, 1)
print(fh)

# Read the file using the handler
csv_path <- system.file("extdata", "clinical_data.csv", package = "DTAtools")
loaded <- read_file(fh, csv_path)
cat("Rows loaded:", nrow(loaded), "\n")
```

---

## `DTADataSetFile`: File Presence and Readability Checks

While `DTADataSetTabular` validates the *content* of a delivered file against a
column column spec and rules, `DTADataSetFile` answers a more basic question:
**did the expected files actually arrive, and can we open them?**

Use `DTADataSetFile` when a DTS requires that certain non-tabular files (PDFs,
archives, reports, audit logs, raw instrument output) are present and
non-empty — without caring about their internal structure.

`check()` for a `DTADataSetFile` verifies each path:

| Check performed       | Failure message                                  |
|-----------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| File exists           | `"File '…' not found."`                         |
| File is non-empty     | `"File '…' is empty."`                          |
| File is readable      | `"File '…' is not readable."`                   |

The same `results()`, `messages()`, and `inspect()` API applies, so you can
report file-level problems alongside tabular column spec errors in a unified
validation summary.

```{r dataset_file}
# Paths to existing files (pass)
delivered_csv <- system.file("extdata", "clinical_data.csv", package = "DTAtools")
delivered_tsv <- system.file("extdata", "gf_data_small_smirna.tsv", package = "DTAtools")

ds_file <- DTADataSetFile(
  name  = "delivery_check",
  paths = c(delivered_csv, delivered_tsv)
)
ds_file <- check(ds_file)
results(ds_file) # both files pass
```

```{r dataset_file_missing}
# Introduce a missing file to trigger a failure
ds_missing <- DTADataSetFile(
  name  = "delivery_check_fail",
  paths = c(delivered_csv, "/nonexistent/path/report.pdf")
)
ds_missing <- check(ds_missing)

results(ds_missing) # one row fails

# The message explains exactly why
messages(ds_missing)[, c("target", "rule_id", "message")]
```

### Declaring the expected files, and binding them as they arrive

`paths =` is the shortcut for files you already have. A specification written
ahead of the delivery instead declares what it *expects*, and each file is bound
with `load_file()` as it turns up — exactly as a tabular dataset is loaded.

The handler for a file that is never parsed is `DTAFileAny` (`type: any` in
YAML). Unlike `DTAFileCSV`/`DTAFileTSV` it carries no reader, which is what lets
a file dataset accept a PDF, an archive or raw instrument output without
pretending it is a table.

Its optional `extensions` restricts which endings are accepted. The list is
**open**, so a delivery of `.xpt` or `.sas7bdat` files needs no change to this
package, and the restriction is applied when the file is offered rather than at
validation time.

```{r dataset_file_load}
ds_declared <- DTADataSetFile(
  name = "declared_delivery",
  files = list(
    DTAFileAny(filename = "clinical_data.csv", extensions = c("csv", "tsv"))
  )
)

ds_declared <- load_file(ds_declared, file = delivered_csv, handler_index = 1)
ds_declared <- check(ds_declared, quiet = TRUE)
validation_status(ds_declared)[, c("table", "status", "ok")]
```

Note the bound target is keyed by the file's **full** name, extension included
(`clinical_data.csv`), which is the name every `results()`, `messages()` and
`inspect()` row for a file dataset reports.

A file whose ending is not allowed is refused up front:

```{r dataset_file_extensions}
pdf_only <- DTAFileAny(filename = ".*", pattern = TRUE, extensions = "pdf")

matches_filename(pdf_only, "study_report.pdf")
matches_filename(pdf_only, "clinical_data.csv")
```

A `DTAFileAny` is only meaningful in a `DTADataSetFile`. A `DTADataSetTabular`
parses everything it is given, so it requires handlers that can actually read
and rejects a reader-less one at construction.

### Mixing `DTADataSetTabular` and `DTADataSetFile` in one `DTA`

A single `DTA` object can contain datasets of both types, letting you validate
the full delivery — column-level content *and* file presence — in one `check()`:

```{r dta_mixed_types, eval=FALSE}
# Tabular dataset (column spec validation)
ds_tab <- DTADataSetTabular(
  name = "clinical_data",
  specs = import_specs_from_yaml(
    system.file("extdata", "gf_dataset.yaml", package = "DTAtools")
  ),
  tables = list(clinical_data = read.csv(delivered_csv))
)

# File dataset (presence check)
ds_fi <- DTADataSetFile(
  name  = "delivery_manifest",
  paths = c(delivered_csv, delivered_tsv)
)

dta_mixed <- DTA(
  datasets = list(ds_tab, ds_fi),
  metadata = DTAMetaData(title = "Mixed DTA", version = "1.0")
)

dta_mixed <- check(dta_mixed)
results(dta_mixed) # one row per dataset
```

---

## The Full DTA Object

### `DTAMetaData`

`DTAMetaData` captures all the administrative information about a DTA:
title, version, contacts (receiver and supplier), and transmission details.

```{r metadata}
# Minimal metadata
meta_simple <- DTAMetaData(title = "My Clinical Data Transmission", version = "1.0")
print(meta_simple)

# Full metadata with contacts and transmission schedule
meta_full <- DTAMetaData(
  title = "Clinical Genomics Data Transmission",
  version = "2.0",
  date = as.Date("2026-01-15"),
  header = "Boehringer Ingelheim",
  receiver = list(
    affiliation = list(name = "External CRO", country = "Germany"),
    contacts = list(
      list(
        name = "Alice Smith", role = "Lead Data Manager",
        email = "alice@cro.com", signature = TRUE, reviewer = TRUE
      ),
      list(
        name = "Bob Johnson", role = "Bioinformatician",
        email = "bob@cro.com", signature = TRUE
      )
    )
  ),
  supplier = list(
    affiliation = list(name = "Pharma Company", country = "USA"),
    contacts = list(
      list(
        name = "Emily Turner", role = "Senior Data Manager",
        email = "emily@pharma.com", signature = TRUE
      )
    )
  ),
  transmission = list(
    type                = "Secure SFTP",
    frequency           = "One-time",
    notification        = "Email",
    date_first_transfer = as.Date("2026-02-01"),
    date_last_transfer  = as.Date("2026-03-31")
  )
)
print(meta_full)
```

### Constructing a `DTA` Object

The `DTA` class holds one or more `DTADataSet` objects together with metadata.

```{r dta_object}
# Build from scratch
ds1 <- create_example_DTADataSetTabular(2) # "demographics" with data
ds2 <- create_example_DTADataSetTabular(3) # "vitals" with data

dta_obj <- DTA(
  datasets = list(ds1, ds2),
  metadata = meta_simple
)
print(dta_obj)

# Access datasets by name or index
datasets(dta_obj, "demographics")
dta_obj[["vitals"]]
dta_obj[c(1, 2)] # returns a list of both datasets
```

### Loading a Full DTA from YAML

The most common production workflow is to define the entire DTA — metadata,
datasets, column specs, rules, and file patterns — in a single YAML file and
load it with `read_dta_from_yaml()`.

```{r read_dta_yaml}
dta_file <- system.file("extdata", "clinical_dta.yaml", package = "DTAtools")
dta_from_file <- read_dta_from_yaml(dta_file)
print(dta_from_file)

# Inspect metadata
metadata(dta_from_file)
```

### Validating a Full DTA

After loading the DTA definition, load data and validate all datasets:

```{r validate_full_dta}
# Get the specs from the DTA
ds_spec_full <- datasets(dta_from_file, "clinical_data")
clinical_sps <- specs(ds_spec_full)

# Load the CSV data
csv_path_full <- system.file("extdata", "clinical_data.csv", package = "DTAtools")
raw_full <- read.csv(csv_path_full)

# Create DTADataSetTabular with specs + data
ds_full <- DTADataSetTabular(
  name   = "clinical_data",
  specs  = clinical_sps,
  tables = list(clinical_data = raw_full)
)

# Validate
ds_full <- check(ds_full)
results(ds_full)
```

## Exporting Data and Documentation

### Write Validated Tables to File

`write_table_to_file()` writes a named table from a `DTADataSetTabular` to disk.
It optionally computes and writes an MD5 checksum sidecar file.

```{r write_table}
# Validate the clinical dataset
csv_path_w <- system.file("extdata", "clinical_data.csv", package = "DTAtools")
dta_obj_w <- read_dta_from_yaml(
  system.file("extdata", "clinical_dta.yaml", package = "DTAtools")
)
ds_w <- DTADataSetTabular(
  name   = "clinical_data",
  specs  = specs(datasets(dta_obj_w, "clinical_data")),
  tables = list(clinical_data = read.csv(csv_path_w))
)
ds_w <- check(ds_w, quiet = TRUE)

# Write to TSV (tab-separated, sorted by SUBJECT_ID)
out_tsv <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
write_table_to_file(
  DTADataSetTabular = ds_w,
  table             = "clinical_data",
  filename          = out_tsv,
  sep               = "\t",
  arrange_by        = "SUBJECT_ID",
  get_md5sum        = FALSE
)
# Confirm output
file.exists(out_tsv)
nrow(read.table(out_tsv, header = TRUE, sep = "\t"))
unlink(out_tsv)
```

Key arguments for `write_table_to_file()`:

| Argument              | Default    | Description                                             |
|-----------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| `sep`                 | `"\t"`     | Field separator (`","` for CSV, `"\t"` for TSV)        |
| `arrange_by`          | `"all"`    | A single column name to sort by, `"all"` to sort by all columns, or `NULL` to skip sorting |
| `compression`         | `"none"`   | `"none"` or `"gzip"`                                   |
| `get_md5sum`          | `TRUE`     | Compute and print the MD5 checksum of the written file  |
| `write_md5sum_to_file`| `TRUE`     | Write MD5 + row/column count to a `.md5` sidecar file  |
| `overwrite`           | `TRUE`     | Whether to overwrite an existing file                  |

### Export Spec Table to Word

Generate a formatted Word table of all column specifications — ideal for
pasting directly into a DTA document.

```{r export_word, eval=FALSE}
# gf_specs was loaded earlier with import_specs_from_yaml()
# Export with default columns: Variable Name, Label, Type, Length, Format, Nullable, Description
docx_out <- tempfile(fileext = ".docx")
export_specs_table(gf_specs, file = docx_out, overwrite = TRUE)
```

Two column layouts are supported:

```{r export_word_layouts, eval=FALSE}
# Layout 1: without Length column
export_specs_table(
  gf_specs,
  file      = "spec_table_short.docx",
  overwrite = TRUE,
  colnames  = c("Variable Name", "Variable Label", "Type", "Format", "Nullable", "Description")
)

# Layout 2: with Length column (default)
export_specs_table(
  gf_specs,
  file      = "spec_table_full.docx",
  overwrite = TRUE,
  colnames  = c("Variable Name", "Variable Label", "Type", "Length", "Format", "Nullable", "Description")
)
```

### Export Column Values Table to Word

Generate a Word table of all allowed values for a specific column — useful for
listing controlled vocabulary in a DTA document.

```{r export_values, eval=FALSE}
# Export all allowed VISIT values for the clinical dataset
docx_values <- tempfile(fileext = ".docx")
dta_obj_export <- read_dta_from_yaml(
  system.file("extdata", "clinical_dta.yaml", package = "DTAtools")
)
clinical_specs_export <- specs(datasets(dta_obj_export, "clinical_data"))

export_column_value_table(
  DTAColumnSpecCollection = clinical_specs_export,
  file = docx_values,
  id = "VISIT"
)
```

### Export the Whole DTA as a Document

`write_dta()` writes the complete agreement — metadata, contacts, transmission
details and every dataset specification — as a Word, PDF or Markdown document.
The format is taken from the file extension unless `format` is given.

```{r write_dta_example, eval=FALSE}
write_dta(dta_from_file, "clinical_dta.docx")

# Route the output through a user-authored Word template instead
write_dta(dta_from_file, "clinical_dta.docx", template = "my_template.docx")
```

Dates in the generated documents are written as ISO 8601 (`YYYY-MM-DD`), so the
same DTA produces the same document regardless of the machine's locale.

#### PDF output

PDF is produced by building the Word document and converting it, which needs an
external tool. `dta_pdf_backend()` reports what this machine will use, and
returns `NULL` when nothing is installed:

```{r dta_pdf_backend_example, eval=FALSE}
dta_pdf_backend()
#> $name
#> [1] "tinytex"
#> $engine
#> [1] "~/.TinyTeX/bin/windows"
#> $available
#> [1] "tinytex" "pandoc"
```

Three backends are tried in order:

1. **LibreOffice** — a `soffice` binary on the `PATH`. Preferred, because it
   renders the document as Word does and keeps table shading, column widths and
   heading numbering.
2. **TinyTeX** — pandoc converts to LaTeX and `tinytex::latexmk()` compiles it,
   installing any missing LaTeX packages on demand.
3. **pandoc** with some other PDF engine already installed.

If none is present, install one from R — no administrator rights required:

```{r install_tinytex_example, eval=FALSE}
tinytex::install_tinytex()
```

`write_dta(format = "pdf")` aborts, naming that command, rather than writing a
DOCX under a `.pdf` name. The output is verified to start with the `%PDF`
signature before it is handed back, so a failed conversion never leaves a
mislabelled file behind.

### Export a Standalone HTML Validation Report

`write_validation_report()` renders a self-contained HTML file — no external
assets, opens straight from disk — summarizing validation results for a `DTA`
object: a pass/fail overview per dataset/target, and a sortable, filterable
table of every validation message with click-to-inspect detail matching the
Shiny app's own validation-messages view.

```{r write_validation_report_example, eval=FALSE}
write_validation_report(dta_from_file, "validation_report.html")
```

Clicking a message row shows what the violated constraint actually requires
and the offending value — the allowed values for an `enum` violation, the
declared type and raw value for an import error, a plain-language description
of a failed rule (built from the rule's own definition), and for
`group_condition` rules, a full breakdown of the group, its conditions and
constraints, and the affected rows' values.

Repeated identical messages (the same violation on many rows) are capped at
`max_repeats` (default `5`) in the default view, with a "show all" toggle in
the file itself so no data is lost:

```{r write_validation_report_max_repeats, eval=FALSE}
# Show at most 10 instances of any repeated message before collapsing
write_validation_report(dta_from_file, "validation_report.html", max_repeats = 10)

# Never collapse repeated messages
write_validation_report(dta_from_file, "validation_report.html", max_repeats = Inf)
```

---

## The Shiny Application

`run_dta_app()` starts a browser interface over the same objects: load a DTA
YAML, upload a data file per dataset, run `check()`, browse the errors, edit the
metadata and export the document — including the HTML validation report above,
via a "Report" download button next to the CSV/TSV/XLSX exports in the
validation-messages dock. Table status in the app reflects all three
validation axes, import errors included.

```{r shiny_app, eval=FALSE}
run_dta_app()
```

The app needs the suggested packages **shiny**, **bslib** and **DT**; if any is
missing, `run_dta_app()` says which to install.

---

## YAML Format Reference

### Column Specification

```yaml
columns:
  # Minimal example — id + type + nullable
  - id: STUDYID
    label: Study Identifier
    type: SAS Char
    nullable: false
    length: 10
    values:
      - 1234-5678
    description: Unique identifier for the study

  # Closed value list
  - id: GENDER
    label: Gender
    type: SAS Char
    nullable: false
    values:
      - Male
      - Female
      - Other

  # Regex pattern (mutually exclusive with values)
  - id: SUBJECT_ID
    label: Subject Identifier
    type: SAS Char
    nullable: false
    pattern: "^SUBJ[0-9]{4}$"

  # Numeric column, nullable
  - id: AGE
    label: Age (years)
    type: SAS Num
    nullable: false
    description: Age in whole years at baseline

  # Nullable character (empty/NA is allowed)
  - id: AE_TERM
    label: Adverse Event Term
    type: SAS Char
    nullable: true
    description: Adverse event verbatim term, empty if no event
```

**Supported types:** `SAS Char`, `SAS Num`, `SAS Int`, `SAS Date`, `SAS Time`,
`SAS DateTime`. The type decides how the column is read as well as how it is
validated — see [Column Specifications](#the-dtacolumnspec-object).

**Nullable values:** `true`/`false` or `Yes`/`No`

### Rules

```yaml
rules:
  # ── col_condition ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # IF CONSENT == "YES" THEN CONSENT_DATE must not be empty
  - id: consent_requires_date
    type: col_condition
    condition:
      CONSENT:
        equals: "YES"
    then:
      CONSENT_DATE:
        empty: false

  # IF VISIT == V03 THEN STATUS must be COMPLETED
  - id: v03_completed
    type: col_condition
    condition:
      VISIT:
        equals: V03
    then:
      STATUS:
        equals: COMPLETED

  # IF GFREASND is populated THEN GFORRES must be empty (mutual exclusivity)
  - id: mutual_exclusivity
    type: col_condition
    condition:
      GFREASND:
        empty: false
    then:
      GFORRES:
        empty: true

  # Multiple then-clauses: age range, weight lower bound, status check
  - id: v03_full_checks
    type: col_condition
    condition:
      VISIT:
        equals: V03
    then:
      STATUS:
        equals: COMPLETED
      AGE:
        min: 18
        max: 65
      WEIGHT:
        greater_equal: 5

  # Pattern matching in condition
  - id: internal_supplier
    type: col_condition
    condition:
      GFREFID:
        pattern: "^Internal_[0-9]+$"
    then:
      GFNAM:
        equals: "Internal"

  # ── col_range ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # AGE must be between 18 and 65 (inclusive)
  - id: age_range
    type: col_range
    column: AGE
    min: 18
    max: 65

  # ── col_unique ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # SUBJECT_ID must be globally unique
  - id: subject_unique
    type: col_unique
    column: SUBJECT_ID

  # The combination of SUBJECT_ID + VISIT must be unique
  - id: subject_visit_unique
    type: col_unique
    column:
      - SUBJECT_ID
      - VISIT

  # ── group_condition ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Within a sample/visit group, failed and reported must not both occur,
  # and failed implies NOT DONE.
  - id: sample_visit_status_logic
    type: group_condition
    group_by: [SUBJIDN, GFREFID, VISIT]
    conditions:
      c1_failed:
        GFREASND:
          empty: false
      c2_reported:
        GFREASND:
          empty: true
        GFORRES:
          empty: false
      c3_not_done:
        GFSTAT:
          equals: NOT DONE
    constraints:
      - id: no_failed_and_reported
        type: mutually_exclusive
        left: c1_failed
        right: c2_reported
        left_scope: any
        right_scope: any
      - id: failed_requires_not_done
        type: requires
        if: c1_failed
        then: c3_not_done
        if_scope: any
        then_scope: all
```

For compatibility with earlier drafts, `not_both` is accepted as an alias for
`mutually_exclusive`, and `implies` as an alias for `requires`.

### Full DTA YAML Structure

A complete DTA YAML file ties together metadata, dataset definitions (with file
patterns), column specs, and rules in a single document:

```yaml
metadata:
  title: Clinical Data Transmission Agreement
  version: "1.0"
  date: 2026-01-15
  header: Boehringer Ingelheim

  receiver:
    affiliation:
      name: External CRO
      country: Germany
    contacts:
      - name: Alice Smith
        role: Lead Data Manager
        email: alice@cro.com
        signature: true
        reviewer: true

  supplier:
    affiliation:
      name: Pharma Company
      country: USA
    contacts:
      - name: Emily Turner
        role: Senior Data Manager
        email: emily@pharma.com
        signature: true

  transmission:
    type: Secure SFTP
    frequency: one-time
    notification: email
    date_first_transfer: 2026-02-01
    date_last_transfer: 2026-03-31

datasets:
  - name: clinical_data
    type: tabular
    description: Clinical subject-level data

    files:
      filename: "clinical_data.*.csv$"
      pattern: Yes
      number_of_files: 1
      type: csv

    columns:
      - id: STUDYID
        label: Study Identifier
        type: SAS Char
        nullable: false
        length: 10
        values:
          - 1234-5678
      - id: VISIT
        label: Visit Code
        type: SAS Char
        length: 12
        nullable: false
        values:
          - V01
          - V02
          - V03
          - EOT
      - id: AGE
        label: Age (years)
        type: SAS Num
        nullable: false
      - id: SUBJECT_ID
        label: Subject Identifier
        type: SAS Char
        nullable: false
        pattern: "^SUBJ[0-9]{4}$"

    rules:
      - id: age_range
        type: col_range
        column: AGE
        min: 18
        max: 65
      - id: subject_visit_unique
        type: col_unique
        column:
          - SUBJECT_ID
          - VISIT
      - id: v03_completed
        type: col_condition
        condition:
          VISIT:
            equals: V03
        then:
          STATUS:
            equals: COMPLETED
```

## API Quick Reference

### Core Classes

| Class                     | Purpose                                                     |
|---------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| `DTA`                     | Top-level container: metadata + multiple datasets           |
| `DTAMetaData`             | Agreement metadata (title, version, contacts, transmission) |
| `DTADataSet`              | Abstract base class for all dataset types                   |
| `DTADataSetTabular`       | Dataset with column specs, rules, and data tables           |
| `DTADataSetFile`          | Dataset that checks file presence and readability only      |
| `DTAColumnSpecCollection` | Named list of column specs + optional list of rules          |
| `DTAColumnSpec`           | Single column definition (type, nullable, values, pattern)  |
| `DTARuleColCondition`     | If/then cross-column rule                                   |
| `DTARuleColRange`         | Numeric range constraint for a column                       |
| `DTARuleColUnique`        | Uniqueness constraint (single or composite key)             |
| `DTARuleGroupCondition`   | Grouped cross-row rule (`mutually_exclusive`, `requires`)   |
| `DTAFileCSV`              | CSV file handler for `read_file()`                          |
| `DTAFileTSV`              | TSV file handler for `read_file()`                          |
| `DTAFileDelim`            | Generic delimited-text file handler for `read_file()`        |
| `DTAFileAny`              | Handler for a file that is never parsed; optional `extensions` |

### Key Functions

| Function                    | Description                                                  |
|-----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `read_dta_from_yaml(file)`  | Load a full DTA (metadata + datasets) from YAML              |
| `read_dataset_from_yaml(file)` | Load a single, self-contained dataset definition from YAML |
| `import_specs_from_yaml(file)` | Load bare column specs + rules from a standalone YAML     |
| `columns_specs_from_word(file)` | Import column specs from a Word table                   |
| `load_file(dta, dataset, file)` | Read a data file into a dataset using its YAML-defined handler |
| `read_file(handler, file)`  | Read a file using a file handler (`DTAFileCSV`, etc.)        |
| `check(x, force, persist, quiet, …)` | Validate all datasets / tables; returns updated object |
| `validate_file_stream(specs, path, …)` | Validate a delimited file by scanning it, without loading it |
| `cache_as_parquet(specs, path, …)` | Rewrite a delimited file as Parquet for repeated validation |
| `results(x)`                | Summary table: status, per-axis error counts per table       |
| `messages(x)`               | Detailed error table: `id`, `source`, row, column, rule, message |
| `inspect(x, id)`            | Deep detail for error `id`: row context, column spec clause, failing rows, original imported text |
| `validation_status(x)`      | Compact status data frame, one row per table                 |
| `validation_errors(x, table)` | Full raw error output for one table                       |
| `clear_validation(x)`       | Discard stored validation state for one or all tables        |
| `metadata_import_errors(x)` | Import errors recorded on a `DTAMetaData` object             |
| `as_r_type(x)`              | R storage type a declared column type maps to                |
| `datasets(x, name)`         | Extract dataset(s) from a DTA object                        |
| `tables(x, i)`              | Extract table(s) from a DTADataSetTabular                    |
| `get_table(x, id)`          | Extract a single Arrow Table by name or index               |
| `specs(x)`                  | DTAColumnSpecCollection from a DTADataSetTabular             |
| `colspec(x, id)`            | Single DTAColumnSpec by column ID                           |
| `rules(x)`                  | List of DTARule objects from a collection or dataset         |
| `metadata(x)`               | DTAMetaData from a DTA object                               |
| `write_table_to_file(…)`    | Write a validated table to disk (TSV/CSV, gzip, MD5)        |
| `write_columns_to_yaml(x, file)` | Serialise specs to YAML                               |
| `write_columns_to_json(x, file)` | Serialise specs to JSON                               |
| `write_dta(x, file, format)` | Write the whole DTA as a document (`docx`, `pdf`, `md`)     |
| `write_validation_report(x, file, max_repeats, …)` | Write a standalone, self-contained HTML validation report |
| `dta_pdf_backend()` | Report the DOCX-to-PDF backend this machine will use, or `NULL` |
| `export_with_template(x, template, file)` | Fill a user-authored Word template from a DTA  |
| `dta_template_placeholders(x)` | List the `{PLACEHOLDER}` tokens a Word template can use, or resolve them for a DTA |
| `export_specs_table(x, file)` | Export spec table to Word                               |
| `export_column_value_table(x, file, id)` | Export value list for a column to Word         |
| `as_json_schema(x)`         | Convert specs to JSON Schema string                         |
| `run_dta_app()`             | Launch the bundled Shiny application                        |

Table names are read with `names(tables(x))`.
